# Jolt (repository)

> Jolt is a Clojure implementation on Scheme: it reads Clojure source, analyzes
> it to a host-neutral IR, emits Scheme, and runs it on Chez (default) or on
> Gambit compiled to JavaScript. The compiler is self-hosted — written in Clojure
> and compiling itself. This file orients a coding agent working inside a clone;
> the user-facing index is at https://jolt-lang.github.io/llms.txt

## There is no JVM here

Jolt targets Clojure semantics, and most portable Clojure runs unchanged, but
nothing below the language is a JVM. Do not reason about JVM behaviour when
debugging jolt code:

- **No Java interop.** No reflection, no `gen-class`, no `proxy`. Interop syntax
  (`Class.`, `Class/staticMethod`, `.method`) resolves against a hand-written
  subset of `java.*` implemented in Scheme under `host/chez/java/`. A class token
  is a name, not a loaded class.
- **The `java.*` shims are convincing but shallow.** A shim implements its JVM
  counterpart's API; it does not bring the JVM's runtime with it. There are no
  classloaders, no JVM GC or heap tuning, and no JVM process-lifetime rules — a
  `java.lang.Thread` does not keep the process alive after the main thread
  returns, and `.setDaemon` is accepted and ignored. If a diagnosis depends on
  JVM runtime semantics, the diagnosis is wrong.
- **Strings are codepoint-indexed** Chez strings. `(count "😀")` is 1, not 2.
- **Regexes** compile through vendored irregex, not `java.util.regex`.
- **`clojure.core` coverage is broad but not total.** A namespace can load with a
  few functions unimplemented.
- **C libraries** are reached through `jolt.ffi` (`foreign-fn`/`defcfn`), not JNI.

The full list is in README.md and in `test/conformance/known-divergences.edn`,
which is the gated registry: `make certify` fails on a new unlisted divergence
and on a stale entry.

## Read first

- [README.md](README.md): what jolt is, install, run, the CLI surface, and the
  full "Differences from Clojure" section.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): building from source, the seed and
  re-minting, architecture, Scheme backends, test gates.
- [test/conformance/known-divergences.edn](test/conformance/known-divergences.edn):
  every tracked jolt-vs-JVM divergence, with a `:legend` explaining each category.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): release history.

## Repository layout

- `host/chez/*.ss`: the Chez runtime — value model, persistent collections, seqs,
  vars/namespaces, reader, host interop. `host/chez/java/` holds the `java.*`
  shims. `host/chez/seed/` is the checked-in bootstrap seed.
- `host/gambit/`: the same overlay on Gambit (second target, also the browser
  build). `host/scheme-adapter/CONTRACT.txt` is the contract between them.
- `jolt-core/jolt/*.clj`: the compiler — reader, analyzer, IR, backend, plus
  `jolt.main` and `jolt.deps`. Baked into the seed.
- `jolt-core/clojure/core/NN-*.clj`: `clojure.core`, in dependency-ordered tiers.
  Baked into the seed.
- `stdlib/`: the rest of the standard library, loaded off the source roots.
- `compatibility/`: namespaces carried so code written for another runtime
  loads unchanged (`cheshire.core` for babashka scripts). Loaded like `stdlib/`.
- `test/`: `test/chez/corpus.edn` is the host-neutral conformance corpus (expected
  values sourced from reference JVM Clojure); `test/conformance/` holds the spec,
  the JVM oracle, and the divergence registry.
- `bin/jolt`: the launcher — run jolt from a clone. (`bin/joltc` is a
  compatibility shim that execs it.)
- `Makefile`: every gate and build target.

## Commands

- `bin/jolt -e EXPR`: evaluate an expression from a clone.
- `jolt FILE [args]`: run a file; with a `#!/usr/bin/env jolt` first line and an
  exec bit it is a script (`./tool arg`). `-f FILE` when the name is also a
  command or a task. `make scriptsmoke` gates it.
- `jolt completions zsh|bash|fish`: a shell completion function to source, so
  `jolt <TAB>` offers jolt's commands and the project's tasks.
  `jolt completions tasks` is the machine-readable listing it calls back for,
  one `name<TAB>doc` per listable task, with a third `cli` field on a task that
  parses its own arguments. `make completionssmoke` gates it.
- `jolt <task>` where the task has an `:exec-fn` or a `:cmd` tree: the arguments
  are parsed by the vendored `babashka.cli` (`vendor/cli`, re-exported as
  `jolt.cli`), so the task gets coercion, validation, subcommands and `--help`
  for free. `jolt org.babashka.cli/completions complete --shell SHELL -- <task>
  <token>…` is the hidden callback the snippets use for those tasks.
  `make taskssmoke` gates it.
- `make test`: the full gate. Individual gates: `corpus`, `unit`, `selfhost`,
  `smoke`, `sci`, `ffi`, `transient`, `certify`, `libconformance`.
- `make remint`: re-mint the bootstrap seed to a byte-fixpoint. Required after
  any change to the reader, the analyzer/IR/backend, `clojure.core`, or one of
  the seven seed-embedded stdlib namespaces.
- `make build`: the standalone `target/release/jolt` binary.

## Gotchas that cost time

- **A seed change without `make remint` silently no-ops.** The checked-in seed
  still carries the old code, and rebuilding the binary does not help. This
  covers `host/chez/reader.ss`, `jolt-core/**`, and the seven `stdlib/`
  namespaces listed in `ei-prelude-ns-files` (`host/chez/emit-image.ss`):
  `clojure.string`, `clojure.walk`, `clojure.template`, `clojure.edn`,
  `clojure.set`, `clojure.pprint`, `clojure.repl`.
- **`make test | tail` reports `tail`'s exit code**, so a failed gate reads as
  green. Capture the make status inside the log instead.
- **Gambit host files are generated** from their Chez counterparts (for example
  `records-gambit.ss` from `records.ss`). Run `make gambitgen` after editing the
  source; `make gambitgencheck` gates the drift.
- **A new `jolt.host` `def-var!` needs a `jolt-host-manifest.txt` line.** Run
  `make manifestcheck` after touching that seam.
- **Documentation does not live in this repo.** Only `README.md`,
  `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and this file. User-facing pages go to the
  site repo (`jolt-lang/jolt-lang.github.io`, `resources/md/` plus a row in
  `resources/docpages.edn`).

## Optional

- [Language specification](https://jolt-lang.github.io/docs/spec/README.html):
  per-form and per-function coverage.
- [RFCs](https://jolt-lang.github.io/docs/rfc/README.html): design notes for
  transients, type hints, inference, compilation modes, program images, and the
  portable Scheme layer.
- [Module map](https://jolt-lang.github.io/docs/MODULES.html) and
  [seed & overlay registry](https://jolt-lang.github.io/docs/seed-overlay-registry.html):
  per-file breakdown of the runtime and the seed.
